feedback: Approved to race. This candidate is valid and is a reasonable step from iteration 1 (232.93) and iteration 0 (238.27, the best raced so far). It changes four things at once: sensor y 0.04 to 0.06 m, mass 0.8 to 0.6 kg, kp 3.5 to 3.0 with kd 0.6 to 0.7, and base_speed 1.5 to 1.4. Each change responds to earlier evidence. Iteration 1 showed that wider coverage cut s-bend and slalom line losses (2.05 to 1.15 and 1.75 to 1.05), but s-bend max_error stayed near 0.063 and oval steering_oscillation rose to 0.29. Because four variables change together, the race will not isolate which one helped. Read the result by metric. If s-bend and slalom line_loss_events fall below about 0.8 and s-bend max_error drops under 0.06, keep the forward sensor shift and the lower mass. If the oval finish rate falls below the 0.40 baseline, the most likely cause is base_speed 1.4, so return it to 1.5 and keep the other changes. If the s-bend still goes off track with max_error above 0.06 and line losses remain high, the next step is a larger kd (about 0.9) or base_speed about 1.3. Do not spend more runs on kp until the speed and damping question is answered.
requested_changes: If the oval finish rate drops below 0.40, set base_speed back to 1.5 and keep sensor y 0.06, mass 0.6, kp 3.0 and kd 0.7. Iteration 0 needed about 1.5 m/s for oval finishes inside 3 s (mean finish 1.87 s at 1.5).

If s-bend max_error stays above 0.06 and line_loss_events stay above 1 per run, raise kd from 0.7 to about 0.9 with kp held at 3.0. Iteration 1 s-bend max_error was 0.0634 and line losses were 1.15 per run.

If line losses on the s-bend and slalom drop but the robot still ends off track on bends, test base_speed 1.3 with the same gains. Iteration 1 showed that line losses were still about 1 per run at base_speed 1.5, so speed is a plausible limiter on bends.
